# FDG8056

> CONSIDER overloading `operator==` and `operator!=` whenever implementing `IEquatable<T>`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.6 IComparable&lt;T> and IEquatable&lt;T>.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library suggestion, application suggestion, test suggestion
- Status: verified

Not machine-checkable as a CONSIDER: for value types CA2231 reports a struct that overrides Equals without the equality operators (FDG8105), and for reference types section 8.13.2 advises against the operators on mutable types (FDG8106) and when they would be much slower (FDG8107).

## From the book

```csharp
public struct Decimal : IEquatable<Decimal>, ... {
   public bool Equals(Decimal other){ ... }
   public static bool operator==(Decimal x, Decimal y) {
     return x.Equals(y);
   }
   public static bool operator!=(Decimal x, Decimal y) {
     return !x.Equals(y);
   }
}
```

See section 8.10 for more details about implementing the equality operators.
